coverage.why: 15 of 17 target venues have a Bandsintown venue page and every event shown on that page's 'Upcoming Concerts' list was captured (the page's own header count, e.g. '52 Upcoming concerts', matched the number of rows rendered — this source does not paginate beyond what loads on first view, unlike a lazy-load city feed). Two venues (The Parish, Summit) returned no matching Bandsintown venue profile after both a targeted domain map search and a site-map crawl of the Austin venue list; Bandsintown's own city-wide venue list for Austin (bandsintown.com/v?city_slug=austin-tx) failed to filter by city on this render (returned New York venues), so venue discovery relied on the Austin city page's embedded venue map plus targeted searches — a systematic gap if either club exists on BIT under a name/spelling not tried.

cityWide.note: The Austin city page renders a genre/date-filtered event feed (All Dates / This Week / This Month tabs) but the page as scraped only exposes an unfiltered, unpaginated slice (~40 rows starting Sep 23) with no visible total count and no way to apply the '30 days' filter without JS interaction the courtesy rules here don't permit (clicking a filter tab). Could not produce a reliable count without either running the filtered URL pattern (bandsintown.com/c/austin-tx/this-month/genre/all-genres) as a second fetch, which time did not allow, or interactive filtering.

linkBehavior: Every venue-page and event-page 'Get tickets' link is a Bandsintown-hosted URL (bandsintown.com/e/<id>-<slug>) that itself redirects client-side to the actual ticketing vendor — the redirect target was not followed (would require a click / browser action out of scope for a courtesy scrape), so ticketUrl and ticketer are recorded as null throughout this file rather than guessed. Bandsintown's own FAQ copy for at least one venue (ACL Live) explicitly separates the BIT event page from its outside vendor (acllive.com box office), confirming BIT is a discovery layer sitting in front of the real ticketer, not the ticketer itself. A 'Remind me' button (as opposed to 'Get tickets') appears on rows Bandsintown has not yet linked to a vendor at all — flagged per-event in notes.
